text:
maria: Quick sync — we need to finalize what KV + prefix-cache metrics the runtime exposes so console/alerts can surface hit rate, evictions, and reuse by workload. Can infra/console/product chime in?
aj: +1. At minimum: hits, misses, evictions, current_entries, and reuse_count. Prefer prometheus counters + gauges so we can roll up easily.
sam: Important: we need to be explicit about labels. model+route+customer_id will explode cardinality. Propose labels: model, route, workload_type (chat/batch), and customer_tier.
lisa: Also include eviction_reason label (e.g., memory_pressure, ttl_expired, explicit_delete) and a histogram for prefix_reuse_count and ttl_before_eviction.
aj: Also would be nice to attach exemplars to eviction events so we can jump to traces when an evict causes a latency spike.
maria: For customer-level analysis, let's avoid raw customer_id on the main metrics. We can expose hashed_cohort/segment for dashboards and provide an infra API for per-customer drilldowns (enterprise only).
neel: From a product POV: console needs per-route hit rate, model-level reuse distributions, and a top-n prefixes by evictions view. Also cohort comparison (free vs paid) and alertable SLIs.
sam: UI idea: time series for hit_rate (stacked by workload_type), stacked area for reuse buckets (0,1-3,4-10,>10), table for top prefixes with evictions and avg_reuse. Make alerts configurable per-route.
aj: Implementation debate: pushgateway vs runtime exposing /metrics. We currently scrape node-level Prom endpoints, but runtime instances are ephemeral — pull still works if we register. OTEL metrics + prometheus exporter could be cleaner.
lisa: Cardinality guards: runtime should aggregate at source for high-cardinality labels. Eg, do not emit per-prefix per-customer raw counters. Emit per-prefix totals and sampled per-prefix-per-route events for debugging.
maria: Proposed metric names and labels (draft):

```
# counters
redwood_kv_cache_hits_total{cache="kv",cache_type="prefix",model="...",route="...",workload="..."} 123
redwood_kv_cache_misses_total{...} 45
redwood_kv_cache_evictions_total{reason="memory_pressure",...} 3
# gauges
redwood_kv_cache_entries{cache="kv",...} 1042
# histograms
redwood_kv_prefix_reuse_bucket{le="1"} 2000
redwood_kv_prefix_ttl_seconds_bucket{le="60"} 500
```
Keep labels: model, route, workload, cache_type, cohort (hashed). Avoid customer_id in the main series.
aj: Agree. Also include an 'ingest_instance' label for aggregation and a small fixed cardinality 'eviction_reason'.
sam: For console panels, I'll mock a dashboard with these panels: 1) Hit rate (1m/5m/1h), 2) Evictions heatmap by reason, 3) Reuse distribution histogram, 4) Top prefixes by evictions (table), 5) SLO panel with alert rules.
lisa: Alerting thoughts: SLI = hit_rate over 5m moving window. Alert when hit_rate < x% AND evictions spike > baseline by 3x. Need runbooks (link to incident playbook) and exemplar traces on alert.
metrics-bot: New metric config PRs should include expected cardinality estimate and a sample query for dashboard owners.
maria: Action items:
- aj: add counters + eviction_reason + TTL histogram to runtime (PR draft) — due EOD Fri
- sam: prototype dashboard in Grafana with mock data, wire to console UX props — due Tue
- lisa: define alert rules and runbook, include exemplar guidelines — due Tue
- neel: write product requirements for the console views and cohorting UX — due Wed
Please react with :thumbsup: if you accept.
aj: ack — will start instrumentation patch and add cardinality estimates to the PR.
sam: ack — will post dashboard mock link once ready.
lisa: ack — will draft runbook and threshold defaults.
neel: ack — will sync with support on useful cohort slices.
maria: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short spec doc and link to this thread for context.
